title: Downsampled per-model latency aggregation and SLO export pipeline
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Goal: Build a production-grade ingestion path for per-model inference latency histograms that balances fidelity and cost, exposes SLOs for realtime alerts, and preserves trace linkage for debugging. Scope: instrument the serving runtime to emit OTel histograms and exemplars, introduce a sampling/downsampling layer that keeps full-label metrics for a configurable fraction of requests, convert selected histogram buckets into Prometheus-compatible metrics for short-term alerting, and write aggregated high-cardinality metrics to long-term store (Cortex/TSDB) for postmortem analysis. Deliverables: (1) runtime changes to emit bucketed latency histograms + exemplars (trace_id, model_id, deployment_id, route); (2) a collector-side downsampler service to retain full labels for ~1% requests per-model and collapse others into aggregated buckets; (3) Prometheus remote_write adapter outputting p50/p95/p99 and burn-rate counters; (4) Grafana dashboards and alert rules (SLO burn rate, sustained p99 regressions); (5) rollout plan and migration docs. Key constraints/decisions: avoid emitting unbounded label sets (owner decided to restrict labels to model_id, deployment_id, tier, and error_class). To preserve debugging fidelity we will keep exemplars (trace ids) sampled at 0.5% globally and 2% for enterprise customers. Storage trade-offs: keep full histograms for 14 days in Cortex and downsample to 1h-rollup for 90d retention. Security/compliance: metrics must not include prompt or PII tokens; runtime scrubs must be enforced. Compatibility: will expose backwards-compatible Prometheus metrics (generated p50/p95/p99 counters and gauge summaries) so existing alerting continues to work. Rollout: opt-in in runtime via feature flag, initial canary to 5% of serving fleet with runtime flag and collector-side routing; compare differences vs baseline OpenTelemetry capture. KPIs: reduction in alert noise, accurate SLO burn rate within +/-5% vs gold-standard offline computation, <2% added tail latency from instrumentation. Links: design doc https://confluence.redwood/obs/per-model-latency-ingest; spike PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1782; collector prototype https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/342; dashboard artifact https://grafana.redwood/d/ABCD123/per-model-latency-slos

2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Implemented runtime histogram emitters (WIP). Introduced bucket schema compatible with OTel histogram v1. Saved initial telemetry to local dev Cortex; observed 1.8% CPU increase on small-scale canary.

2025-02-14 - Claire Ng (review): Reviewed prototype PR. Feedback: (a) ensure exemplars include trace_id only, not span attributes; (b) add toggle to disable exemplars per-tenant for compliance-sensitive customers. Logged review comments on PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1782#review.

2025-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Collector-side downsampler service MVP done. It groups incoming OTel metrics by (model_id, deployment_id, route) and applies reservoir sampling for label retention. End-to-end tests added. Prototype deployment to staging: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/342

2025-02-18 - Ops: Deployed canary to 5% of hosting fleet (staging). Observed increase in remote_write throughput ~12% but compression reduced net storage growth to ~3% due to collapsed buckets. Noted two models with extremely high cardinality (custom-customer tags) — created ENG-21905 to address label hygiene.

2025-02-20 - Data Science: Compared exported p95/p99 from Prometheus short-term metrics against offline gold histograms. Median error for p95 was 3.2%, p99 4.7% — within target but need more sampling for low-traffic models. Action: add adaptive sampling per-model based on traffic volume.

2025-02-22 - Aisha Patel: Preparing rollout checklist. Items: finalize feature flag gating, add per-tenant exemplar opt-out, update runbook (alert playbook), schedule canary to 20% next week. Created dashboard panels for SLI burn rate and exemplar sampling yield.
